name: Savery’s fire engine for raising water
description: Savery described a water-raising engine using steam condensation to draw water into a vessel and steam pressure to force it out.

date.basis: Publication year on the title page of the source transcription.

events.statement: In The Miner’s Friend, Savery described a fire-driven water-raising engine using condensation and steam pressure.
events.caveats: This is the date of the published description, not the date of invention or proof of a successful mine installation.

evidence.locator: Title page; Chapter First, Manner of Working the Engine
evidence.supports: Publication year and operating description: steam condenses, water rises into a vessel, and steam pressure forces it out.

earliest_record.rationale: The 1702 publication is the earliest source-backed record established in this bounded research; no claim of earliest invention or prior use.

caveats: The account is the inventor’s own promotional description; this record does not establish influence on Newcomen or an actual mine installation.

research.note: Direct reading of a transcription of Savery’s 1702 account. Independent admission review pending.
